title: Hatter's Quince and Chestnut Tarts
tagline: Tiny tarts, jammy centres, and a cloud of chestnut cream.

ingredients.item: ripe pear, peeled and coarsely grated

steps: Rub the butter into the flour, icing sugar and salt until it looks like breadcrumbs. Stir in the beaten egg, bring together into a dough, wrap and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Roll the dough to 3 mm thick, cut 8 cm rounds, and press them into a 12-hole bun tin. Re-roll scraps as needed. Chill the tin.
Tip the quince paste, grated pear and lemon juice into a small pan over a low heat. Stir for 4 to 5 minutes until soft and jammy. Cool for 5 minutes.
Spoon the filling into the pastry cases, about a heaped teaspoon each. Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the pastry is golden at the edges.
Cool the tarts in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift out onto a rack. Beat the mascarpone and chestnut purée until smooth and spoon a dollop onto each cooled tart.
image_prompt: A mismatched china plate of twelve small round shortcrust tarts with golden fluted edges, each filled with glossy amber quince and pear jam and topped with a soft swirl of pale beige chestnut cream. A few tarts sit on a cake stand beside a teacup, with a dusting of crumbs on the plate.
alt_text: Small golden jam tarts with glossy amber quince filling and swirls of chestnut cream on a china plate beside a teacup.
caption_hook:
Jam tarts, but make them autumnal. Quince and pear underneath, chestnut cream on top, and no one has stolen any yet.

Which would you grab first, the tart or the teacup?
